method: Read-only manual assessment against each actual recorded prompt and changed-line chunk. The supplied prefix and generated continuation are kept separate. Valid JSON syntax, runtime citation validation, exact expected location, causal correctness, and termination are assessed independently. A correct paraphrase earns semantic credit; awkward grammar alone does not erase a supported failure mechanism.
what_prefix_supplies: The top-level findings key, a nonempty findings array, and the start of its first object/key. The concern branch is externally imposed. The model supplies key names, line IDs, reason text, any additional findings, closing syntax and EOS.

cases.prompt_scope_note: The actual recorded prompt includes root, tools, and tools/archive rules, but not the sibling tools/docs rule from the source fixture. This probe cannot demonstrate sibling-scope discrimination.

conclusion: Forcing the positive branch does not by itself recover reliable reviews: one of four continuations provides a grounded concern, and that one uses an exact training prompt. Two invent unavailable citation IDs; one cites an available causal line but explains the wrong mechanism. The control shows some conditioned explanation ability without establishing autonomous concern detection.
limits: All four cases contain a concern and all receive an externally supplied positive prefix. This probe provides no independent verdict score, clean false-positive rate, or concern/clean pair success. It does not replace the prior unforced result. The same fixed four prompts and prefix can be compared with the new selected checkpoint.
independent_second_read: A second read-only reviewer reached the same four judgments, including semantic credit for the null-guard mechanism despite poor grammar.
